head_commit.message:
pm-249/t-1569: Accept a live sha that contains EXPECT_SHA or trails it by report-only paths

The live probe failed at 9d0167a, a report-only commit. The push
paths-ignore (projects/**, **.md) keeps that commit from deploying. Main
keeps one pending CI run, so a newer push replaced ec59663's run 448 (it
was cancelled), and the live sha can only reach it as a descendant.

verify-deploy.sh now passes when /api/health serves EXPECT_SHA, a
descendant of it, or an ancestor that trails it only by projects/* and
*.md. Ancestry is read from the checkout, and an unknown served sha is
fetched from origin once. A stale deploy with code pending, a sha off
another branch and an unknown sha still exit 1. The self-test grows to
15 checks against a temporary git fixture, with a code-lead stale deploy
as the new negative control. ci-workflow.test.mjs pins the report-only
patterns to ci.yml's paths-ignore. The README and the t-1569 summary are
updated to match.

display_title: pm-270/t-1604: Drive the probes with locked playwright-core and the r…

head_commit.message:
pm-270/t-1604: Drive the probes with locked playwright-core and the runner's Chrome

Run 40307460821's "Motion probe, signed in" spent 866 s, against 171-180 s
when green, before its first assertion: npm i playwright@1.64.0 and
playwright install chromium --only-shell --with-deps (apt-get plus a CDN
download) ran silently into the 20-minute job budget. Main then bumped
the budget to 35 minutes, which hid the stall without naming it.

- scripts/probe-browser.mjs launchBrowser(): an explicit PW_PREFIX wins,
  loading require("playwright") from that prefix. Otherwise the repo's
  playwright-core launches channel "chrome". With neither, one error
  names both causes. The module loader is injectable.
- scripts/probe-browser.test.mjs (in npm test), with a fake loader:
  Chrome when PW_PREFIX is unset, PW_PREFIX's playwright when set, clear
  errors for a missing Chrome, a missing playwright-core and an empty
  prefix, and real resolution of the locked playwright-core.
- probe-motion-signed-in.{sh,mjs} and probe-end.{sh,mjs}: with CI set
  and google-chrome on PATH nothing is installed. Otherwise the old
  temp-prefix installers run (and embedded-postgres for the motion
  probe), each under timeout 180 (a perl alarm without coreutils), with
  date -u stamps and the exit status on stdout.
- ci.yml: checks timeout-minutes 35 -> 20, with a comment citing the
  measured green steps (10-11 min). Motion probe, Footer walk and
  Footer Chromium probe each get timeout-minutes 8.
- next.config.ts: rewrite /favicon.ico to /icon.svg. Under the runner's
  Chrome the motion probe failed the same check twice ("plain 403
  (router.push from /dashboard) -> /dashboard by the nav's Dashboard:
  no page error and no console error"). The cause was Chrome's fallback
  request for /favicon.ico, which 404'd. The Chromium headless shell
  never makes that request. No probe assertion changed.

Run here (Linux lease, docker Postgres, Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57,
TMPDIR=/tmp):
- motion probe, CI=1, Chrome, before the rewrite: 355 ok / 1 failed,
  twice (191 s with build, 156 s without)
- control, no CI, temp-prefix playwright with Chromium shell 156: 356 ok
  / 0 failed, 173 s (npm i 1 s, playwright install 11 s)
- motion probe, CI=1, Chrome, after the rewrite: 356 ok / 0 failed,
  172 s with build, 157 s with SKIP_BUILD
- footer probe, CI=1, Chrome: 171 ok / 0 failed, 56 s
- /favicon.ico answers 200 image/svg+xml; /nope still 404
- npm test 2233/2233, lint and typecheck exit 0

display_title: pm-249/t-1569: Verify the deployed sha, terminal and press after each…

head_commit.message:
pm-249/t-1569: Verify the deployed sha, terminal and press after each production deploy

scripts/verify-deploy.sh BASE_URL EXPECT_SHA polls /api/health until its sha
equals the full 40-hex EXPECT_SHA (default 300 s, capped at 590 s). It then
runs e2e/pocket-terminal.test.ts and e2e/ink-press.test.ts against BASE_URL
through scripts/e2e.mjs. A sha that never matches, a non-200 answer or a
failing e2e exits 1, and bad arguments exit 2.

--self-test drives the script against a local fake /api/health with a
stand-in e2e. Negative control: a sha mismatch exits nonzero and never
reaches the e2e. The other controls cover a sha that turns right mid-poll,
HTTP 500, nothing listening, a failing e2e, and EXPECT_SHA=dev or a
missing BASE_URL (both refused). The checks job runs the self-test.

pm-270's scripts/vercel-deploy.sh had already replaced the bare health
curl. The production job now runs verify-deploy right after it with
EXPECT_SHA=$GITHUB_SHA against https://otohime.dev, and timeout-minutes goes
from 12 to 18 to fit the e2e (about 107 s live). A ci-workflow test
requires that step after the deploy and refuses a bare health curl.
README documents the script.

head_commit.message:
pm-270/t-1605: Bound the Vercel production deploy and assert the served sha

Run 40311256064's blocking `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` hung 850 s
until the 15-minute job timeout, with no public state and the health
check skipped; that check only asserted 200.

scripts/vercel-deploy.sh replaces the deploy and health steps:
- upload with --no-wait under a 300 s bound; retry once only on a fast
  failure with no deployment URL, never after a timeout or once a URL exists
- `vercel inspect <url> --wait --timeout 6m --logs` under a 420 s bound;
  on failure re-read the state and print ::error title=vercel deploy::<state> <url>
- /api/health (HEALTH_URL) must report "sha":"$GITHUB_SHA"
- bounds use GNU timeout (process group), a perl fallback on macOS

scripts/vercel-deploy.test.sh drives it with a fake npx: 25 checks
including a hanging upload failing in 4 s with one deploy call and no
leftover child, a hanging inspect printing "Building after 2s <url>",
a healthy deploy, and a health body for another sha failing. It runs in
the checks job; production timeout-minutes goes 15 -> 12.

display_title: pm-270/t-1606: Make the desk swipe observe its preconditions and carr…

head_commit.message:
pm-270/t-1606: Make the desk swipe observe its preconditions and carry a gesture trace

e2e/desk.test.ts swipe() now scrolls the tape into view, waits until its box
holds still across two animation frames, and asserts that the element at its
centre is the tape. It takes { holdMs, drags }. With drags it waits for
[data-dragging] on the item after the first touchMove past DRAG_THRESHOLD and
for that attribute to clear after touchEnd. Without drags it asserts that the
attribute never appears. Every swipe asserts that its pointerdown and its
pointerup or pointercancel reached the page. Only waiting conditions are used,
no fixed sleep.

New scripts/e2e-gesture-trace.ts (pure, unit-tested in
scripts/e2e-gesture-trace.test.ts, now part of npm test) keeps at most 40
pointerdown/move/up/cancel records. When the list is full it drops moves
first. It also formats the records. A capture listener in the page's
instrument() feeds it, and the trace appears in the assertion message of the
wide-desk control (the 120 px drop is unchanged), the touch-tablet no-drag
check and the narrow-window mouse no-drag check.

Nothing is quarantined: no run showed an environmental cause or a valid
gesture lost inside ink-desk.tsx, so the application is unchanged.

e2e against a production build with a docker Postgres
(scripts/e2e-local.sh, local macOS, Chrome channel): 3 of 3 runs passed,
110/110 tests each. Negative control: with the tablet swipe set to
drags: true, the suite failed 109/110 with "music is dragging after the
first move past 6px" followed by the pointer trace.

display_title: pm-268/t-1599: Carry print runs through every public root layout

head_commit.message:
pm-268/t-1599: Carry print runs through every public root layout

Every root layout (and the global 404) mounts the same small appearance
boundary: AppearanceBoot in <head> renders that root's token aliases,
generated from the trusted presets, plus a pre-paint script that validates
the two storage keys exactly as the store does. AppearanceRuntime in <body>
keeps <html> markers and tagged SVG filters in step with the store, other
tabs and bfcache restores. House adds no attribute, property or layer.

SVG adapters tag source values (data-ap-frequency/scale/seed) on figures,
season bits, Ink Press, Ink Radio, ledger stamps, the 404 crumple and the
Ryugu caustic; the runtime rescales them after hydration and restores the
exact source text on reset. One static texture layer sits behind the page
within the 0.06 alpha budget, pointer transparent, off in forced colors.

Isolation tests gain an exact allowlist for the two boundary components in
each root layout, with positive and negative controls.
